title: Create and activate a Python virtual environment on macOS
summary: A virtual environment is a private folder with its own Python and pip. Create one in your project and activate it in Terminal, so packages you install stay inside it and do not touch the system Python.

aliases.text: how to activate virtualenv on mac
активировать виртуальное окружение python на маке
как включить venv в терминале mac

prerequisites: Terminal open in your project folder

steps.explain: Check which python3 Terminal runs. The path is usually /usr/bin/python3 (Apple's Command Line Tools), /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (Apple Silicon Homebrew) or /usr/local/bin/python3 (Intel Homebrew). If macOS offers to install developer tools, accept, then run this step again.
steps.expect: A path such as /usr/bin/python3 or /opt/homebrew/bin/python3. Nothing printed means Python 3 is missing.

steps.explain: Create the environment in a folder named .venv inside the project. It gets its own copy of Python and pip. The command prints nothing when it works.

placeholders.name: VENV_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder for the environment, usually .venv inside the project folder

steps.expect: No output. A folder named <VENV_DIR> appears in the project folder.

steps.explain: Activate the environment in this Terminal window. After this, python and pip point to the environment, and the prompt starts with the folder name in brackets. Activation lasts only until you close the window or run deactivate.

placeholders.name: VENV_DIR
placeholders.description: The environment folder created in step 2

steps.expect: The prompt starts with (.venv) or the folder name you used.

alternatives.explain: The same activation written with a single dot. Some tutorials use this form; it does the same thing in zsh.

placeholders.name: VENV_DIR
placeholders.description: The environment folder created in step 2

alternatives.expect: The prompt starts with (.venv) or the folder name you used.

steps.explain: Install a package into the active environment. python -m pip always uses the pip of the Python that is running, so the package goes into the environment.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Name of the package to install from PyPI

steps.expect: The last line starts with 'Successfully installed' and names the package.

steps.explain: Leave the environment when you are done. The prompt loses the bracketed folder name and python goes back to the system or Homebrew Python.
steps.expect: The (.venv) prefix disappears from the prompt.

verify.expect: The full path of the environment folder, for example /Users/you/Projects/myproject/.venv.

warnings: Do not run 'sudo pip install': it installs into the system Python instead of the environment.
Each new Terminal window needs the activate step again. Packages stay in the folder, so you do not reinstall them.
